goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:81 — `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)` matches the raw query-string URL byte-for-byte against the RSS `i.link` stored by PollFeed, so trailing-slash/scheme/case/fragment/utm differences never match and the embed shows "Loading" forever while RetrieveTopic imports a duplicate topic per URL variant (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact string equality on `embed_url` (e.g., `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` and `TopicRetriever` checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`). `Jobs::PollFeed` imports using `i.link` / `i.id` without any canonicalization, so URL variants (scheme/case/trailing slash/query/fragment) will not match and can lead to duplicate `TopicEmbed`/topics for the “same” page. The “Loading forever” part is not strictly guaranteed by the diff (the async fetch_http path could eventually create the missing embed), but the underlying exact-match URL keying/duplication risk is real and introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:16 — check-then-insert (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then PostCreator + `create!`) races between concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed jobs; the unique index turns the loser into a RecordNotUnique raise after topic creation work instead of an idempotent upsert (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a check-then-act: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent imports for the same `url` (e.g., `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`Jobs::PollFeed`) can both observe no row and race; the loser will hit a `RecordNotUnique` on `create!`, turning the operation into an exception rather than an idempotent “already imported” outcome. The diff does not show any rescue/upsert to handle this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` compares an unnormalized setting (case, `www.`, trailing port) against the parsed host, so a setting like `Example.com` or `example.com:8080` rejects every legitimate embed; same drift at lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the check `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` compares the parsed referer host (a hostname only) against the raw `embeddable_host` setting string with no normalization. From the diff, `embeddable_host` is defined as a free-form string in `config/site_settings.yml`, so values like `Example.com` (case mismatch) or `example.com:8080` (includes port) would not equal `URI(...).host` and would cause legitimate embeds to be rejected. The same direct string comparison exists in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously re-downloads and re-imports the entire feed on every cache miss (unthrottled for staff via `no_throttle`), coupling per-URL retrieval to a full hourly batch and amplifying load for each unknown embed_url (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the current `@embed_url` is not yet in `topic_embeds` (it checks existence before and after). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) fetches `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and iterates/imports every item, so this is a synchronous full-feed poll triggered by a per-URL embed cache miss. The per-URL throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) keys on `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` and can be bypassed via `no_throttle` (set for staff in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), so staff requests could cause repeated full feed downloads. This is a concrete load/architecture concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:21 — `feed_key` is computed but never used, so there is no Last-Modified/ETag short-circuit and every poll materializes and SHA1-diffs every feed item (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is defined (computes a Redis key based on the feed URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in the diff. The actual polling logic (`poll_feed`) always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates every item, with no conditional GET / caching / short-circuit shown. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded efficiency/architecture issue rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:81 — `topic_id_for_embed` returns a topic_id with no FK or deleted_at check, so an embed whose topic/post was deleted permanently resolves to a dead topic and never re-imports (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is implemented as `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` with no join/validation that the referenced `topics`/`posts` rows still exist. The migration also adds `topic_id`/`post_id` columns without foreign keys, so a stale `topic_embeds` row could exist. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out early on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, which would prevent re-import if such a stale row exists. However, the diff does not show deletion behavior (whether `TopicEmbed` rows are removed when a topic/post is deleted), so the dead-record scenario is plausible but not provably occurring from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — update path `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` only rewrites the body; a changed feed `title` is silently never propagated to the topic (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an embed already exists (`embed.present?`), the update path only revises the post body via `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` and updates `content_sha1`. The passed-in `title` is not used to update the associated `topic` (or first post title), so a changed feed/item title from `Jobs::PollFeed` (which calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) will not be propagated. This contradicts the stated intent of “Creates and Updates Topics based on an RSS or ATOM feed.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `default: 1` is a magic int implicitly coupled to `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` ordering in app/models/post.rb:64; reordering the enum silently flips every existing post to raw_html (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` with `default: 1` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb) and defines `Post.cook_methods` via `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb). This does implicitly couple the DB default integer to the enum’s positional mapping; if the enum order were changed later, existing rows with value `1` would map to a different semantic. However, as shown, the current mapping is consistent (default 1 corresponds to the first enum value), so it’s not a present defect in this PR—it's a maintainability risk created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx` followed by separate `$redis.expire` is non-atomic; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or errors between these calls, the key can remain without an expiration, making `retrieved_recently?` return `true` indefinitely for that `@embed_url` (permanent throttling). This is directly verifiable in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place, so the injected "Imported from" footer leaks into caller-owned data (e.g. Readability/RSS item objects) (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the passed-in `contents` String in place, which is a real side effect on caller-owned data (Ruby Strings are mutable and `<<` mutates). However, in the shown call sites the argument is typically a fresh String (e.g., `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `doc.content` in `import_remote` is immediately consumed), so the diff does not demonstrate an actual broken behavior—it's a maintainability/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — The spec expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve to be called synchronously, but app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 only enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic, so the "no previous embed" path has no valid verification and the test fails or proves nothing. (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct: in `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when no topic is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever` nor calls `retrieve`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` on the “no previous embed” path. This mismatch means the spec will fail (or at least is verifying behavior that does not exist in the controller).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — The raw_html cook_method returns unsanitized feed/remote HTML as cooked, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 renders it with `raw`, so XSS from imported content has no sanitization and no test. (P0, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where sanitization typically occurs). `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` create posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using HTML content sourced from RSS/remote (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The added spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) even asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming unsanitized HTML is expected and there is no test asserting sanitization against script/event-handler injection. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:66 — absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative `//host/x` links as root-relative and rewrites them to `http://embedhost/host/x`, and no spec covers this obvious edge case. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links are rewritten when href/src `start_with?('/')` and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` is applied. A protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/x` also starts with '/', so it will be rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x` (where `prefix` comes from the article URL, e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`), which is incorrect behavior for protocol-relative URLs. The existing spec only covers single-slash root-relative paths (`/hello`, `/images/...`) and does not cover `//host/...`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:61 — The port check drops explicit non-default ports only for 80/443 no matter the scheme (for example https on port 80 or http on port 443 are mishandled), and nothing verifies it. (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix logic appends the port only when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This ignores the URL scheme: for `https://host:80/...` or `http://host:443/...`, the port is non-default for that scheme but will be dropped because it matches 80/443. That yields incorrect absolute URLs. The existing spec only covers default-port examples (`http://eviltrout.com/...`) and does not verify port edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:1 — Rendering uses the TopicView `best: 5` option but ignores sibling gating on that path (deleted/hidden posts, whisper/moderator_action post types, and a topic the current_user cannot see), so embeds can leak content with no acceptance criteria or test. (P1, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbedController#best building a TopicView with `{best: 5}` and the view iterating `@topic_view.posts`, but it does not show TopicView’s implementation or whether it filters deleted/hidden/whisper/moderator_action posts or enforces topic visibility via a Guardian. Since those behaviors are not present in the diff, the claim that this path “ignores sibling gating” and “can leak content” is not verifiable from the PR changes alone (the view merely renders what TopicView provides).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The revise path adds skip_validations but never carries or checks cook_method or bypass_rate_limiter (passed at app/models/topic_embed.rb:37), so the options passed during updates are only partly honored and the update spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40 does not check re-cooking or the sha1 update. (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows PostRevisor now honoring `skip_validations` via `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, so the claim that options are only partly honored (at least for skip_validations) misreads the change. The assertion that `bypass_rate_limiter` is “never carried or checked” cannot be verified from the provided diff hunks because only a small portion of `lib/post_revisor.rb` is shown and it may be handled elsewhere in that file. While the spec does not assert the embed record’s `content_sha1` update, the finding’s core claims about ignored options are not verifiable from the diff as given.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:38 — poll_feed itself (item link/id fallback, missing user, content scrub, non-http ids) has no test, so feed import is unverified. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` contains nontrivial parsing and normalization logic (e.g., `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterating `rss.items`, choosing `i.link` vs `i.id`, rejecting non-`http(s)` URLs, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and returning early if `embed_by_username` user is missing). However, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only verifies the `execute` preconditions and that it delegates to `poll_feed` (it even stubs `poll_feed`), and does not exercise or assert any of the `poll_feed` behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — `i.content.scrub` raises on RSS items that only have `description` (content nil), so the whole feed stops importing, and no fallback or test exists. (P1, conf 75)
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content.scrub` will raise when RSS items lack `content` (nil) and only have `description`, and notes missing fallback—this is the same nil-pointer/crash risk described in the golden comment, including the suggested fallback concept.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — The `--category` option is removed without a replacement, so Disqus imports silently lose category assignment, which is a regression of existing behavior. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept or set a category, so Disqus imports can no longer be assigned to a category via the CLI as before (a behavior regression). Note: if a user still supplies `-c/--category`, Thor would now likely error as an unknown option rather than silently ignore it, but the loss of category assignment capability is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — The referer host must exactly match embeddable_host, so `www.` subdomains, ports, and https/http variants fail, and the embed_url host is never checked against embeddable_host in the controller. Neither case is covered by specs. (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by an exact host equality check: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so a `www.` variant (or any other subdomain) will be rejected unless the setting matches exactly. Also, the controller does not validate `params[:embed_url]` against `embeddable_host` before enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (the host validation happens later in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), which can lead to pointless enqueues/rendering `loading` for mismatched `embed_url`. The controller specs only cover missing host, missing referer, and happy-path, and do not cover these edge cases. (Note: the finding’s claim about ports and http/https variants failing is not supported here because `.host` ignores scheme and port.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targets the full `request.referer` as origin, which is invalid when the referer includes a path in some browsers and is blank when there is no referer, and the iframe resize contract is unverified. (P2, conf 50)
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that postMessage is using the full `request.referer` as the targetOrigin, which is invalid when it includes a path (and can be blank), causing the message to be rejected/dropped—matching the golden issue that targetOrigin must be just the origin (scheme+host+port) to allow resizing messages through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads forever every 30s when retrieval fails (invalid host, missing embed_by_username user), because there is no terminal or error state and no acceptance criterion. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders the 'loading' template. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb unconditionally reloads the page every 30s via setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000). If the background retrieval can never create a TopicEmbed (e.g., TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early when SiteSetting.embed_by_username user is missing, or other retrieval failures), the embed URL will continue to have no topic_id and the client will loop reload indefinitely with no terminal/error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Editing an already-shipped migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` means any environment re-running it (schema reload, re-migrate after version-table loss) silently DROPs and recreates top_topics, discarding all computed rows, while environments that already ran it never see the change, producing drift (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it when the migration is run, which can cause silent data loss on schema reloads or in cases where migrations are re-applied. Because this is an edit to an already-existing migration (not a new corrective migration), environments that already ran the old version will not get the change, creating drift while others may experience destructive behavior on rerun.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true do |t|` silently drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table and its data instead of failing loudly on conflict, making re-runs destructive (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table before recreating it. If the migration is re-run (or the table already exists for any reason), this is destructive and can silently cause data loss rather than failing on conflict. This behavior is directly shown in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5 — `t.integer :topic_id, null: false` / `t.integer :post_id, null: false` have no foreign keys or indexes, so deleting topics/posts leaves orphaned topic_embeds whose `embed.post` is nil and TopicEmbed.import then crashes in PostRevisor.new(nil) for that URL forever, since the unique embed_url row blocks re-creation (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` but only adds a unique index on `embed_url` (no FK constraints and no indexes on the associations). In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` row is found it does `post = embed.post` and, on content changes, unconditionally runs `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revise!`. If the referenced post has been deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil`, making this path crash or at least fail hard. Because `embed_url` is unique, the stale/orphaned `topic_embeds` row also prevents re-creating a fresh mapping for the same URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a change to `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`, but it is purely whitespace/newline churn (e.g., removing trailing spaces after `disable_ddl_transaction!` and touching the final newline) with no functional change to the migration logic. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, which exists only in Ruby 2.1+, and SimpleRSS returns nil content for plain RSS items that only have <description>, so the hourly poll raises NoMethodError and imports nothing (P1, conf 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote calls `open(url)` but only poll_feed.rb requires 'open-uri'; when that file is not loaded (dev without eager loading, disqus.thor), Kernel#open treats the URL as a file path and raises Errno::ENOENT (P1, conf 50)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — The new raw_html cook_method bypasses the cooking/sanitization pipeline for imported posts, which turns "URL handling and validation" into skipping content validation entirely (P1, conf 50)

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` sets the throttle key before `perform_retrieve` runs, so when the fetch/import fails, retries from non-staff viewers do nothing for 60s while the loading page keeps reloading. (P2, conf 100)

But `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` *before* `perform_retrieve` runs. If `perform_retrieve` (e.g., `fetch_http` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) fails to create an embed, subsequent calls within 60s will return `true` from `retrieved_recently?` and skip `perform_retrieve`, delaying retries while the loading page (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) keeps reloading every 30s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `setnx` and `expire` are separate calls, so a crash between them leaves a `retrieved:` key with no TTL and that URL is throttled forever. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling is implemented with two non-atomic Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes (or loses connectivity) after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is set, the `retrieved:` key can persist without a TTL, causing `setnx` to keep failing on future requests and effectively throttling that URL indefinitely. The diff shows no cleanup path for such a stuck key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` has no timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge remote page can tie up a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and use unbounded memory. (P1, conf 100)

This method is invoked from background jobs (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and feed/disqus import paths), so a slow server or very large response can block a Sidekiq worker and potentially consume unbounded memory while reading the full body into a string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout or size cap, and with `retry: false` any network or parse error kills the whole hourly poll without any retry. (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network fetch via open-uri with no explicit timeouts or size limits and no exception handling. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any transient network error, hang, or parse exception will fail that scheduled execution without Sidekiq retrying it, preventing feed import for that interval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — `rss.items.each` has no per-item rescue, so one bad item (nil `i.content` makes `.scrub` raise, or `TopicEmbed.import` fails) stops the loop and every later feed item is skipped with no error handling. (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop `rss.items.each do |i|` directly calls `i.content.scrub` and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item error handling. If an item has `i.content == nil` (making `.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`) or if `TopicEmbed.import` raises for any item, the exception will abort the entire job and skip all subsequent feed items. This is exacerbated by `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad item can prevent later items from ever being imported until the next successful run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError on RSS 2.0 items that only have `description` and no `content`, so polling fails for common feeds. (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code unconditionally calls `i.content.scrub` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). If `SimpleRSS.parse` returns items where `content` is nil (e.g., feeds that only provide `description`), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub` and abort polling. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the whole feed fetch and import inline inside every uncached embed retrieval, so a feed error blocks the `fetch_http` fallback and many parallel viewers set off many feed polls. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and only then proceeds to `fetch_http` (after checking whether the embed now exists). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no error handling. Any exception from `open`/parsing will bubble up and prevent `fetch_http` from running, so a feed outage/bad URL can break embed retrieval even though the HTTP readability fallback could have succeeded. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — when `creator.create` returns a post with errors or nil, the transaction commits with no TopicEmbed and `import` returns quietly, so the embed shows "Loading" forever and each new retrieval creates a duplicate topic. (P1, conf 75)

However, the finding’s stronger claim (that a topic is nonetheless created, causing duplicates and “Loading forever”) is not directly verifiable from this diff because `PostCreator#create`’s persistence/return semantics aren’t shown here. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `revisor.revise!` returns false on failure but its result is ignored, and `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs anyway, so the failed update is recorded as applied and never retried. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, it unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` immediately after calling `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb, around the `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` block). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 — `post = embed.post` can be nil when the post was deleted, so `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises and the feed poll crashes on every run. (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed row is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then (if content changed) unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revise!`. Since there is no DB-level foreign key shown and no guard, `embed.post` can be `nil` if the referenced Post was deleted, causing an exception and potentially breaking scheduled/feed import runs that hit that embed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` changes the caller's string in place, and a frozen or already-appended string raises or shifts the SHA1, so identical content keeps being revised. (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the passed-in String in place before computing `content_sha1` (`Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`). The diff does not show any current caller reusing a single String instance (PollFeed and import_remote appear to pass freshly-created strings), so the “identical content keeps being revised” claim isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the in-place mutation concern itself is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` raises when the embedded topic was deleted or is not visible to the user, so the iframe gets a raw 500/404 page instead of an embed fallback. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — every uncached embed request enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job and the loading page reloads every 30s, so a busy page with N viewers enqueues N jobs every 30 seconds with no dedup at enqueue time. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — `document.location.reload()` repeats every 30s forever with no attempt limit or backoff, so a URL that permanently fails to import leaves the iframe polling forever. (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the script calls `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`. While it only schedules one reload per page load, each reload re-renders the same template (when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is still nil in `EmbedController#best`) and re-schedules another reload, resulting in indefinite 30s polling if the import never succeeds. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — the resize postMessage only fires once on `window.onload`, so later content or image loading changes the height without a new message and the iframe (`scrolling="no"`) cuts off comments. (P3, conf 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:58 — `absolutize_urls` calls `URI(url)` without a rescue, so a feed item link that passes the `^https?://` regex but is malformed raises URI::InvalidURIError and stops the import loop. (P2, conf 50)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — embed_url param is never validated against embeddable_host before enqueuing a remote fetch, so the headline validation requirement is not actually met (P1, conf 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses the cooking/sanitization pipeline, so attacker-controlled HTML from the RSS feed or a fetched page (script tags, onerror handlers, javascript: hrefs) is stored and rendered verbatim as a post across the whole forum, which is stored XSS (P0, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/filtering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), and since `cook` returns `raw`, the stored cooked HTML will be attacker-controlled verbatim. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` puts unsanitized raw_html post content into an iframe served with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL on the Discourse origin, so any script in imported content runs with the forum's cookies (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a pathway for storing and rendering un-sanitized HTML as-is. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and RSS/feed imports set `cook_method: :raw_html` and pass `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` with `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The embed view then renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any `<script>`/JS in imported feed content will execute in the iframe on the Discourse origin. `EmbedController` explicitly sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), enabling this content to be framed by the configured host; it does not mitigate script execution. `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls `i.content` from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and does not sanitize it before import (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), making XSS realistically reachable if the feed/content is attacker-controlled or compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `"#{url}"` interpolates the feed-supplied URL into HTML without escaping, so a link like `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(1)` injects attributes and markup into a raw_html post (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")` to `contents` without any HTML escaping or sanitization of `url`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quote/attribute injection (e.g., `http://x/'onmouseover='...`). Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, this injected markup would be rendered as-is, making this a verifiable XSS risk from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` uses open-uri on a URL taken from the embed_url request param, and TopicRetriever only compares the host, so an attacker picks any port and path on that host, and open-uri follows redirects to internal addresses such as 169.254.169.254 or localhost; the response is then published as a post (SSRF) (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) on a URL that originates from the `embed_url` request param in `EmbedController#best` (params.require(:embed_url) -> Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...) -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`). `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not constrain scheme/port or prevent following redirects. Since `open-uri` follows redirects by default, a crafted URL on the allowed host/path could redirect to internal addresses (e.g., 169.254.169.254/localhost), resulting in SSRF and publishing fetched content as a post via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is Kernel#open, so a value starting with `|` runs a shell command and `file:///etc/passwd` reads local files into posts; an admin, or a compromised admin session, reaches command execution (P2, conf 50)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:22 — The "not a url" test passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host defaults to '' which already differs from any host, so the rescue branch is not actually proven (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicRetriever#invalid_host? the logic is `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` with a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` returning true. In the spec "does not call perform_retrieve when the embed url is not a url", `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is not stubbed, and the default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `embeddable_host: ''`. So the test doesn’t specifically validate the rescue branch behavior (it only validates that invalid inputs skip retrieval). This is a test coverage/precision issue, not a product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40 — Update-path test only checks cooked =~ /new contents/, which passes even if cook_method raw_html is lost on revision or content_sha1 is not updated; the unchanged-sha no-op branch (topic_embed.rb:34) is untested (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial update logic in TopicEmbed.import: when an embed exists it only revises the post if content_sha1 changed, and then updates embed.content_sha1 via update_column (app/models/topic_embed.rb, else-branch and `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). The spec’s update test (`Supports updating the post`) only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/`, which would still pass even if the sha tracking were broken (e.g., embed.content_sha1 not updated) because the post revision happens before the sha update. Also, the no-op path when `content_sha1` is unchanged is not covered by any test in the added spec, as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — New save(validate: !skip_validations) behavior has no test proving invalid content is saved with skip_validations and rejected without it (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing new behavior controlled by `skip_validations` (lib/post_revisor.rb). While TopicEmbed.import uses `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, the added/updated specs (e.g., spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) only assert that updates work, not that validations are actually bypassed when `skip_validations: true` and enforced when absent/false.
